2026-09-09.title: #cD542: Snabbit’s 15-Minute Beauty Fix
2026-09-09.articleText:
How long does it take for you to get a basic threading or quick hair-styling done before a last-minute office presentation or an evening event? Traditionally, it meant calling a local salon hours in advance, travelling through traffic, or waiting for a scheduled home-salon technician to arrive in a 2-hour delivery window. Bengaluru-based startup Snabbit is upending this status quo by taking the "instant" ethos of quick-commerce and applying it directly to personal grooming.

• Snabbit initially built its core engine around hyper-local, on-demand domestic home services, aggregating and formalising household cleaning, chores, and maintenance.

• By focusing on ultra-dense neighborhood micro-markets, Snabbit achieved sub-15-minute fulfillment times for daily household chores.

• Having raised over US$112 million, including a massive Series D round, the company is now executing a natural category expansion- instant, salon-at-home services.

The business logic behind Snabbit’s foray into beauty is rooted in customer overlap and purchase frequency.

• While traditional at-home beauty models rely on planned, high-ticket packages with long appointment wait times, Snabbit targets high-frequency, low-ticket daily beauty needs such as threading, waxing, quick facials, and saree draping

• Its strategy hinges on supply-side innovation- beauty professionals are cross-trained into multi-skilled service providers capable of handling multiple tasks in a single session.

• Combined with lightweight, single-use monodose kits from premium brands like O3+ and Rica, workers can travel light and complete jobs rapidly within a tight geographic radius.

Operating on a unit-pricing revenue model starting as low as Rs.49 with no minimum order requirements, Snabbit extracts platform commission while maximizing the daily utilization rates of its all-women service workforce. This instant-fulfillment beauty vertical deepens platform stickiness, converting occasional app users into daily active consumers who rely on Snabbit for both house cleaning and quick personal grooming.

For business, marketing, and operations graduates, the rise of instant home services creates entry-level roles across vendor acquisition, micro-market operations, supply chain management, and growth marketing. Building density in neighborhood clusters demands field-level execution, customer engagement, and tactical partner management.

2026-09-10.title: #cD543: Atulya’s Grey Hair Goldmine going Global
2026-09-10.articleText:
Imagine an elderly Tamil couple living in Mauritius, requiring specialized geriatric care and daily assistance. Local facilities lack culturally aligned services, while family members balancing demanding careers find it challenging to provide full-time care. This gap represents the emerging landscape of global eldercare.

• Indian assisted-living operators are expanding into overseas markets to address this demand.
• Driven by an aging global population, the senior care sector is evolving into a cross-border healthcare and real estate asset class.
• World Health Organization expects to see the over-60 demographic cross 22% of the total population.

Leading this international expansion is Morgan Stanley-backed Athulya Senior Care. The Chennai-based firm is setting up its "Chez Moi" facility in Mauritius alongside plans for Sri Lanka and Dubai.

• The business strategy targets specific demographics: the Tamil diaspora in Mauritius and Sri Lanka for familiar cultural care, and Dubai for high-net-worth Indian expatriates navigating the local real estate ecosystem.
• Simultaneously, Athulya has signed MoUs with Singapore’s SingHealth and Japan to export skilled geriatric care manpower.
• By combining asset-light operational tie-ups abroad with specialized workforce export, Indian eldercare companies are addressing global talent shortages while unlocking higher margins.

The underlying business model relies on turning operational capacity into scalable, high-yield revenue streams.

• Athulya currently manages 1,500 beds (900 operational), generating Rs.8.5 crore monthly.
• With India's organized senior care market projected to expand from 20,000 to 100,000 units by 2030, Athulya is targeting a Rs.1,000 crore top-line and Rs.250 crore EBITDA to support a planned FY32 IPO.

For fresh management graduates, this cross-border evolution creates opportunities across client acquisition, cross-border operations, regulatory compliance, and business development. Scaling a high-touch service delivery model across international jurisdictions requires professionals who can navigate complex international healthcare partnerships, manage cross-cultural workforce deployment, and drive client-facing engagement.

Cadabams, a pioneer in senior living and mental healthcare, recently offered an early-career opportunity for campus talent. However, no students chose to nominate for the selection process. Missing out on a pioneer in an industry projected to scale from US$15 billion to US$50 billion within a decade represents a lost opportunity to enter a high-growth sector early.

What do you think about this missed opportunity?

2026-09-11.title: #cD544: Kirloskar’s Avante Spaces
2026-09-11.articleText:
What happens when a 135-year-old engineering behemoth known for industrial pumps, engines, and heavy machinery steps decisively onto prime urban terrain? Through its real estate arm, Avante Spaces, Kirloskar Industries Group is sharpening its focus on commercial, residential, and mixed-use developments. Beginning with Pune - a bustling hub for technology, manufacturing, and institutional real estate - Kirloskar joins a powerful cohort of Indian conglomerates like Tata, Godrej, L&T, and Mahindra that are turning legacy corporate land banks into resilient, long-term growth platforms.

The underlying business logic driving this shift is institutionalization.

• Over the past decade, Indian real estate has transitioned from a fragmented, local trade into a structured, highly regulated corporate asset class governed by RERA guidelines, REIT vehicles, and institutional capital standards.
• Global and domestic investors demand high governance standards, long-term balance sheet strength, and sustainable architectural design.
• Avante Spaces recently raised Rs.1,150 crore in rupee term loans to fund its commercial footprint in Pune, which boasts ~2 million square feet of development potential.
• By leveraging its brand heritage alongside flexible deal structures such as Joint Ventures (JVs), Joint Development Agreements (JDAs), and direct acquisitions, the group scales without tying up excessive internal equity.

For business and management graduates, this wave of institutional corporate real estate redefines early-stage career paths.

• Entry-level opportunities span market research analyst, lead generation specialist, and client acquisition manager within enterprise B2B sales.
• Securing Fortune 500 tenants or large IT firms for a 1.7-million-square-foot office tower requires consultative selling, strategic negotiation, and deep key-account management.

Starting a sales or market research career with dynamic regional developers - such as Rohan Corporation for residential and commercial assets in Tier-2 hubs like Mangaluru - provides invaluable ground-level training in consumer psychology, site sourcing, channel partner networks, and deal closures.

Mastering regional market dynamics builds the core execution muscle required to transition seamlessly into enterprise B2B roles at conglomerate giants like Kirloskar, managing complex multi-million-dollar leasing portfolios and institutional accounts across major metropolitan markets.

2026-09-10.articleText:
Imagine an elderly Tamil couple living in Mauritius, requiring specialized geriatric care and daily assistance. Local facilities lack culturally aligned services, while family members balancing demanding careers find it challenging to provide full-time care. This gap represents the emerging landscape of global eldercare.

• Indian assisted-living operators are expanding into overseas markets to address this demand.
• Driven by an aging global population, the senior care sector is evolving into a cross-border healthcare and real estate asset class.
• World Health Organization expects to see the over-60 demographic cross 22% of the total population.

Leading this international expansion is Morgan Stanley-backed Athulya Senior Care. The Chennai-based firm is setting up its "Chez Moi" facility in Mauritius alongside plans for Sri Lanka and Dubai.

• The business strategy targets specific demographics: the Tamil diaspora in Mauritius and Sri Lanka for familiar cultural care, and Dubai for high-net-worth Indian expatriates navigating the local real estate ecosystem.
• Simultaneously, Athulya has signed MoUs with Singapore’s SingHealth and Japan to export skilled geriatric care manpower.
• By combining asset-light operational tie-ups abroad with specialized workforce export, Indian eldercare companies are addressing global talent shortages while unlocking higher margins.

The underlying business model relies on turning operational capacity into scalable, high-yield revenue streams.

• Athulya currently manages 1,500 beds (900 operational), generating Rs.8.5 crore monthly.
• With India's organized senior care market projected to expand from 20,000 to 100,000 units by 2030, Athulya is targeting a Rs.1,000 crore top-line and Rs.250 crore EBITDA to support a planned FY32 IPO.

For fresh management graduates, this cross-border evolution creates opportunities across client acquisition, cross-border operations, regulatory compliance, and business development. Scaling a high-touch service delivery model across international jurisdictions requires professionals who can navigate complex international healthcare partnerships, manage cross-cultural workforce deployment, and drive client-facing engagement.

Cadabams, a pioneer in senior living and mental healthcare, recently offered an early-career opportunity for campus talent. However, no students chose to nominate for the selection process. Missing out on a pioneer in an industry projected to scale from US$15 billion to US$50 billion within a decade represents a lost opportunity to enter a high-growth sector early.

What do you think about this missed opportunity?

2026-09-09.articleText:
How long does it take for you to get a basic threading or quick hair-styling done before a last-minute office presentation or an evening event? Traditionally, it meant calling a local salon hours in advance, travelling through traffic, or waiting for a scheduled home-salon technician to arrive in a 2-hour delivery window. Bengaluru-based startup Snabbit is upending this status quo by taking the "instant" ethos of quick-commerce and applying it directly to personal grooming.

• Snabbit initially built its core engine around hyper-local, on-demand domestic home services, aggregating and formalising household cleaning, chores, and maintenance.

• By focusing on ultra-dense neighborhood micro-markets, Snabbit achieved sub-15-minute fulfillment times for daily household chores.

• Having raised over US$112 million, including a massive Series D round, the company is now executing a natural category expansion- instant, salon-at-home services.

The business logic behind Snabbit’s foray into beauty is rooted in customer overlap and purchase frequency.

• While traditional at-home beauty models rely on planned, high-ticket packages with long appointment wait times, Snabbit targets high-frequency, low-ticket daily beauty needs such as threading, waxing, quick facials, and saree draping

• Its strategy hinges on supply-side innovation- beauty professionals are cross-trained into multi-skilled service providers capable of handling multiple tasks in a single session.

• Combined with lightweight, single-use monodose kits from premium brands like O3+ and Rica, workers can travel light and complete jobs rapidly within a tight geographic radius.

Operating on a unit-pricing revenue model starting as low as Rs.49 with no minimum order requirements, Snabbit extracts platform commission while maximizing the daily utilization rates of its all-women service workforce. This instant-fulfillment beauty vertical deepens platform stickiness, converting occasional app users into daily active consumers who rely on Snabbit for both house cleaning and quick personal grooming.

For business, marketing, and operations graduates, the rise of instant home services creates entry-level roles across vendor acquisition, micro-market operations, supply chain management, and growth marketing. Building density in neighborhood clusters demands field-level execution, customer engagement, and tactical partner management.

2026-09-11.articleText:
What happens when a 135-year-old engineering behemoth known for industrial pumps, engines, and heavy machinery steps decisively onto prime urban terrain? Through its real estate arm, Avante Spaces, Kirloskar Industries Group is sharpening its focus on commercial, residential, and mixed-use developments. Beginning with Pune - a bustling hub for technology, manufacturing, and institutional real estate - Kirloskar joins a powerful cohort of Indian conglomerates like Tata, Godrej, L&T, and Mahindra that are turning legacy corporate land banks into resilient, long-term growth platforms.

The underlying business logic driving this shift is institutionalization.

• Over the past decade, Indian real estate has transitioned from a fragmented, local trade into a structured, highly regulated corporate asset class governed by RERA guidelines, REIT vehicles, and institutional capital standards.
• Global and domestic investors demand high governance standards, long-term balance sheet strength, and sustainable architectural design.
• Avante Spaces recently raised Rs.1,150 crore in rupee term loans to fund its commercial footprint in Pune, which boasts ~2 million square feet of development potential.
• By leveraging its brand heritage alongside flexible deal structures such as Joint Ventures (JVs), Joint Development Agreements (JDAs), and direct acquisitions, the group scales without tying up excessive internal equity.

For business and management graduates, this wave of institutional corporate real estate redefines early-stage career paths.

• Entry-level opportunities span market research analyst, lead generation specialist, and client acquisition manager within enterprise B2B sales.
• Securing Fortune 500 tenants or large IT firms for a 1.7-million-square-foot office tower requires consultative selling, strategic negotiation, and deep key-account management.

Starting a sales or market research career with dynamic regional developers - such as Rohan Corporation for residential and commercial assets in Tier-2 hubs like Mangaluru - provides invaluable ground-level training in consumer psychology, site sourcing, channel partner networks, and deal closures.

Mastering regional market dynamics builds the core execution muscle required to transition seamlessly into enterprise B2B roles at conglomerate giants like Kirloskar, managing complex multi-million-dollar leasing portfolios and institutional accounts across major metropolitan markets.
